blocks.title: Backtracking
blocks.text: Backtracking builds a solution step by step; if a path does not lead to a solution, it goes back and tries a different path, like turning back on a map when you are going the wrong way.
It is used for problems that need all possible options to be considered, such as puzzles and combinations.

blocks.prompt: Explain backtracking with reference to the N-Queens problem (long question 5).
blocks.explanation: Place N queens on an N x N board so that no two share a row, column or diagonal. Place one queen per row, starting at the first row; in each row try the columns from left to right and keep the first safe one, then move to the next row. If a row has no safe column, go back to the previous row, move that queen to its next safe column and continue. When all N rows are filled, a solution is found; trying every option this way finds all solutions. For N = 4 there are 2 solutions, for example queens in columns 2, 4, 1, 3 of rows 1 to 4. Backtracking prunes a branch as soon as it fails, so it explores far fewer configurations than trying every arrangement.

items: Backtracking: build step by step, go back at a dead end; N-Queens is the classic example.
